summary: Diagnostics standalone capture/enable can accept a forged or duplicate direct child that copies a valid WorldEntityId and fidelity, because directRepresentations selects any direct child with the identity attribute and preflightReadouts only resolves the record plus fidelity/adornee. Unlike PhysicsLabValidation, this boundary does not prove unique entity IDs, canonical recipe membership/name, or representation identity before publishing a readout. The 20-cycle runToggleEvidence path is protected later by captureFull, but the manual enable/capture evidence surface can become non-canonical. Recommend a one-shot source hardening lane after the active diagnostics primary lands: fail closed on duplicate/foreign representations before any diagnostics allocation and regression-lock the rejection without claiming Studio evidence.
evidence: main@aa7e04f05834ae783773c908fccfdbbe510558e5 src/server/PhysicsLab/PhysicsLabStudioDiagnostics.luau: directRepresentations includes every direct child whose UNRENDERED_WorldEntityId attribute is non-nil.

preflightReadouts resolves lab.getRecord(entityId), compares only UNRENDERED_Fidelity with the authoritative record, and finds an adornee; it does not reject duplicate IDs or verify the child name/recipe identity against the canonical PhysicsLab recipe.
capture repeats the same permissive selection and can therefore publish multiple EntityDiagnostic rows for one authoritative record or a row attached to a foreign child carrying copied attributes.

src/server/PhysicsLab/PhysicsLabValidation.luau already rejects duplicate WorldEntityIds, unexpected representation keys, recipe mismatches, and wrong canonical representation geometry, proving the stronger invariant exists elsewhere but is not applied by standalone diagnostics enable/capture.

Active diagnostics work #295/#301/#304 covers bounded cycle input, lifecycle/no-drift ordering, and failure-atomicity documentation; repository search found no existing finding for forged/duplicate diagnostics representation trust.
